newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds seen wandering in ranges again on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Bunds seen wandering in ranges again on Friday.

text.p: Bund futures are expected to remain stuck in their recent range on Friday after shrugging off a flury of official pronouncements on European monetary union to dip in line with Treasuries in Thursday.

Traders said there is little clear direction to the German debt market and are looking for clear signals about the strength of the German economy before pushing the Bund futures contract out of its recent range of about 60 basis points.
At 1424, the DTB Bund futures contract was down 14 basis points at 100.16, after trading in a range between 100.02 and 100.39 on the day.

"The market is on a bit of a knife-edge," said Stuart Trow, bond market analyst at Norinchukin International in London. "Nobody knows if we are going to move toward setting fresh highs or fresh lows." Bunds, as has been the case recently, showed little reaction to a stream of comments about the prospects for European moentary union.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel and his deputy Juergen Stark, stressed in speeches that Germany would rein in its budget deficit to achieve EMU entry. "Germany will fulfil the criteria," Waigel told a savings bank conference. "Even current developments give no cause to veer from these forecasts."
"On the face of it, EMU should be bad for Bunds, but the market is not taking any notice now," one analyst said.
Bunds, meanwhile, continued to outperform Treasuries, pushing the spread to 113 basis points from 111 at the close on Wednesday.
Analysts said the gains were mostly due to the long-end of the yield curve catching up with recent outperformance on the short and middle part of the yield curve.
Although both the German and U.S. economy appear to be gathering steam, Treasuries face more pressure than Bunds, raising some expectations of further Bund outperformance.
Trow said he would not be surprised to see the Bund/T-note spread move toward 117 basis points or even higher over the medium-term.
The benchmark 10-year cash Bund was down at 100.65 from 100.71 on Wednesday to yield 5.90 percent.
With few domestic indicators due, the market's focus is on a pair of U.S. indicators scheduled for Friday -- retail sales and producer prices at 1230 GMT.
